metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice exactly matches the prediction of the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. The experimental design contains many trials where TTB and Tallying make diametrically opposite predictions (e.g., TTB strongly favors A because of the highest validity cue, whereas Tallying favors B because it has a greater number of less valid cues). By computing the TTB match rate, we expect a score close to 1.0 for simulated TTB agents, and a score well below 0.5 (often close to 0.2) for Tallying agents.

This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the strict preference of the Tallying heuristic. The experimental design specifically pits Tallying against Take The Best (TTB) such that on all trials where Tallying has a strict preference, TTB prefers the exact opposite option (driven by the highest-validity discriminating cue). Therefore, Tallying agents will score significantly above 0.5, while TTB agents will score significantly below 0.5.
